subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Ductus Venosus, Biophysical Profile, NST and CTG

steps.tx: Flow reversal during atrial contraction in the fetal venous shunt, the **ductus venosus a-wave**, signals failing cardiac compensation. In early growth restriction it is the strongest Doppler predictor of stillbirth. Absent or reversed a-wave at viable gestation usually triggers delivery. The a wave reflects atrial contraction against a stiff heart, and reversal means pressure in the atrium is rising.
steps.say: A reversed ductus venosus a-wave signals failing compensation and usually triggers delivery.

steps.tx: The five component ultrasound and heart rate assessment scoring fetal wellbeing is the **biophysical profile**. Breathing, movement, tone, fluid and heart reactivity each score two points. Scores of eight to ten reassure, zero to four demand delivery. A score of six is equivocal and earns a repeat within hours, not routine review next week.
steps.say: The biophysical profile scores five components, with eight to ten reassuring.

steps.tx: Recording fetal heart accelerations with movement without contractions is the **non-stress test**. Two accelerations in twenty minutes make it reactive and reassuring. It is the antenatal test of choice for most high risk surveillance. A sleeping fetus can stay non reactive for forty minutes, so the test is extended before calling it abnormal.
steps.say: The non-stress test seeks two accelerations in twenty minutes for reassurance.

steps.tx: Continuous electronic recording of fetal heart and contractions is **cardiotocography**. Baseline, variability, accelerations and decelerations are read systematically. Interpretation frameworks classify traces as reassuring, non reassuring or abnormal. A baseline of 110 to 160 with variability 5 to 25 and no decelerations is the reassuring pattern to quote.
steps.say: Cardiotocography records heart and contractions read systematically by four features.

steps.tx: Beat to beat fluctuation of the baseline between five and twenty five beats is **baseline variability**. It is the single most reassuring CTG feature when normal. Reduced variability with decelerations is the most ominous combination. Saltatory variability above 25 beats can precede compromise and is not read as reassuring excess.
steps.say: Baseline variability is the most reassuring CTG feature when normal.

steps.tx: The systematic reading mnemonic covering contractions, baseline, variability, accelerations, decelerations and overall impression is taught as **DR C BRAVADO**. It prevents missed features in a pressured labour ward. Documentation follows the same sequence every time. DR C BRAVADO ends with an overall plan, because a feature list without a decision helps nobody.
steps.say: DR C BRAVADO systematises CTG reading so no feature is missed.

steps.tx: A reactive trace needs accelerations, whose absence alone is not pathological in a sleeping fetus, termed the **sleep cycle caveat**. Fetal sleep lasts up to forty minutes with quiet variability. Extending monitoring usually captures wakefulness. Vibroacoustic stimulation or a drink of cold water often wakes the fetus and shortens the test safely.
steps.say: Absent accelerations may reflect fetal sleep lasting forty minutes, so monitoring extends.

steps.tx: Combining Doppler and biophysical testing in early growth restriction follows **integrated surveillance**. Umbilical changes come first, then cerebral, then venous, then biophysical deterioration. This sequence times delivery to the last safe moment. Venous Doppler changes typically precede an abnormal biophysical score by about a week in early restriction.
steps.say: Integrated surveillance follows the Doppler to biophysical deterioration sequence for timing.

steps.tx: Antenatal CTG has high false positive rates, so abnormal traces prompt **confirmatory assessment**. Reviewing the whole clinical picture, scalp stimulation or blood sampling refines decisions. Unnecessary caesareans follow blind trace reaction. Fetal scalp blood sampling is now rare, replaced by faster delivery decisions when traces stay pathological.
steps.say: Abnormal antenatal traces need confirmatory assessment because false positives are common.
